sources.citation: Bhat, D. N. Shankara. 1966. Studies in Tulu. Bulletin of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute 25 (Silver Jubilee volume, 1965-66): 11-31. [Dialect comparison of Tulu caste dialects -- Brahmin, Bunt, Jain, Pujari, Holeya, Koraga, Kudiya -- from fieldwork at Peradala village, Kasaragod taluk; sec. 2 comparative phonology.]
sources.note: Nothing. All 21 pages read by eye from 200-dpi page renders: six topics, all segmental and comparative-historical (A:B correspondences between the Sivalli Brahmin and Sapaliga dialects of Udupi incl. phoneme inventories, loss of initial short vowels and syncope in dialect B; merger of PDr. *c/*t in non-Brahmin dialects with reflexes t/c/s/h/zero; palatalization of *k in the Koraga dialect of Peradala; *i,*e > u,o after labials before retroflexes; reflexes of PDr. *r; absence of SDr. i/e u/o alternation). The words stress, accent, tone, pitch do not occur and no statement about word prominence…

sources.note: Inventory only: SPPEL has issued no grammatical sketch or 'grammatical features' page for Kudiya (sketches exist only for Luro, Sanenyo, Eravalla; features pages for 20 other languages). Open audio of isolated words exists but no analysis.

sources.citation: Joseph, Nidhin. 2024 [fieldwork 2014]. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Kudiya Language in Karnataka and Kerala. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2024-007. Dallas: SIL International. 33 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4 (printed p.6, p.12): 'There is a lack of documentation and analysis of the Kudiya language. During their preparation period, the researchers could not find any published sources about the Kudiya language.' Sec. 5 (p.9): 'There is virtually no documentation of the Kudiya language and very little is known about it.' Appendix A (pp.11-19): 210-item IPA wordlists for Kudiya G1 (Poomala clan, Kodagu) and K1 (Thenmala clan, Kasaragod) plus Kodava; no stress marks anywhere.

sources.citation: Mohanagowda, H. [ಮೋಹನಗೌಡ ಎಚ್.]. 2011. ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಕನ್ನಡ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆಯ ಮಲೆಕುಡಿಯರು: ಸಮಾಜೋ-ಸಾಂಸ್ಕೃತಿಕ ಅಧ್ಯಯನ [The Malekudiyas of Dakshina Kannada district: a socio-cultural study]. PhD thesis (guide D. R. Panduranga, Rashtrakavi Govinda Pai Research Centre, Udupi), Kannada University, Hampi. In Kannada. Section 3.7.7 'ಭಾಷೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ' (Language and literature), printed pp. 76-95.
sources.note: Nothing. The language section gives sociolinguistic remarks, lexical shibboleths between sub-groups (kaipu vs aamra 'vegetable curry', arbunchaar 'river'), then a morphological sketch of Tulu 'with the Malekudiyas' Tulu words in view': personal pronouns compared across Dravidian, case suffixes 1-8 with example sentences, numerals; the only prosodic remark is that the vocative is formed by lengthening the noun's final vowel. No phoneme inventory, no word stress, no tone.
